[SG Android] Add policy logging for Enterprise Proxy.

Introduce the ENTERPRISE_PROXY log source to PolicyLogger and emit
policy logs for enterprise proxy operations. This records policy
updates, configuration refreshes, network and account change triggers,
cache events, and detailed fetch errors in EnterpriseProxyService and
ProxyProvisioningDomainManager. Also expose
ProvisioningDomainStateToString for formatted log messages and add unit
tests verifying the emitted logs.

[lens-overlay] Re-enable text highlights in region-only mode.

Previously, text highlights were disabled in selected region only mode
because bounding box coordinates received from the server response were
aligned to the selected region, not to the viewport. Corrects this by
storing the selected region coordinates and using them to translate
received coordinates back to the viewport, allowing text highlights to
be restored in selected region only mode.

Allows the WebUI to fall back to regionTextResponse when
fullTextResponse is unavailable. Since the fullTextResponse is not
available in region-only mode, text highlights were previously not
appearing even when the data was available in the regionTextResponse.
Adds checks for a zero-length regionTextResponse to prevent inadvertent
clearing of the context menu when this fallback happens.

zoom_scale is removed from CreateGeometryMojomFromProto because it
caused incorrect behavior whenever not equal to 1. The scaling
represented by zoom_scale was already being performed on the values in
region_crop_box->crop() by the server, so it was not necessary to
scale again on the client.

[ChroMenu] Pre-refactor search bar to use standard Textfield focus

Prepare AppMenuSearchBarView for standard MenuHost FocusManager focus
management:
- Remove custom FocusBarView caret and key event forwarding from
  AppMenuSearchBarView; rely on views::Textfield's native cursor and
  focus state instead.
- Install FocusRing on the outer search container; FocusRing's default
  predicate already checks parent()->HasFocus() when no custom predicate
  is set.
- Update AppMenuSearchBarViewTest and ActionAppMenuTest to focus the
  search field via FocusManager when testing focus-dependent UI state.

This CL does not introduce any typing capabilities. The search bar is
not interactable. This is purely a preparatory CL in order to ensure
plumbing can be done sequentially.

[ChroMenu] Fix zoom menu item crash via touchscreen

When the page reaches minimum or maximum zoom, the corresponding `-` or
`+` button in `AppMenuZoomView` becomes disabled. If the user taps the
disabled button via touch (or clicks the empty area of the zoom row),
the unhandled event falls through to `MenuController`, which accepts the
enclosing `kActionZoomSubmenu` `MenuItemView` and calls
`ActionAppMenu::ExecuteCommand(kActionZoomSubmenu, ...)`. Because
`kActionZoomSubmenu` is a custom container row whose actions are handled
by its child views, passing it to `ActionAppMenuMetrics::LogMenuAction`
hits a `NOTREACHED()` crash.

8bac2ff61dde1f8a9e9e0b25393bfd68c46ffa1c [ diff ] 
WebXR: Fix swapchain state for unrendered composition layers

When a WebXR frame does not render into a composition layer:
1. XRGPUTextureArraySwapChain::OnFrameStart() and
   XRWebGLTextureArraySwapChain::OnFrameStart() only reset the wrapped
   swap chain's texture_queried_ flag without calling the base
   OnFrameStart(), leaving texture_was_queried() permanently true after
   the first frame and submitting a cleared texture on skipped frames.
2. OpenXrGraphicsBinding::ReleaseActiveSwapchainImages() skips releasing
   a layer's active swapchain image when !layer->is_rendered() so the
   image can be reused on the next frame, but
   OpenXrLayers::AddCompositionLayer() only checked
   layer.needs_redraw(), causing xrEndFrame to reference a dynamic
   swapchain whose active image was not released for that frame.
3. OpenXrGraphicsBinding::WaitSwapchainImages() skipped calling
   OnSwapchainImageReady() when reusing an already-waited active
   swapchain image from an unrendered frame.

Reset texture_queried_ in the texture-array wrapper swap chains, check
layer.is_rendered() in AddCompositionLayer(), and invoke
OnSwapchainImageReady() when reusing an active swapchain image.

[PopupCreator] Ensure POPUP CustomTabActivity is closable across all windowing modes

POPUP CCTs force-disable the toolbar close button because a desktop
window's OS caption bar already provides one. When Chrome lacks
REPOSITION_SELF_WINDOWS the popup falls back to a regular task, and
on tablets, phones and in fullscreen there is no caption bar, so the
popup cannot be closed by the user.

Stop clearing isCloseButtonEnabled() for POPUP in the intent data
providers, so the close button exists like in any other CCT, and have
CustomTabToolbarCoordinator's existing AppHeaderObserver toggle it via
CloseButtonVisibilityManager.setVisibility(!isInDesktopWindow) on
toolbar init and on every desktop-windowing transition.
MinimizedFeatureUtils also excludes POPUP, since minimizing a child
window to PiP is misleading.

Covered by
PopupMultiwindowPTTest#testPopupToolbarCloseButton_matchesWindowingMode.

[ash] Drop dead //chrome includes from ash code (1/4: ash UI)

Twenty includes across chrome/browser/ui/ash and
chrome/browser/ui/webui/ash name nothing from the header they pull in:
profile_manager.h (11), browser_process.h (5) and
app_service_proxy_factory.h (4).

These three headers were picked because each is only ever reached by
name -- ProfileManager::, g_browser_process, AppServiceProxyFactory:: --
so a file that never writes the symbol cannot be using it. That is not
true of every header: a type held in an auto variable is used without
being named, which is why browser_window_interface.h is left for a
separate pass.

Candidates were removed wholesale, then chrome, unit_tests,
browser_tests and interactive_ui_tests were built, and everything the
compiler rejected was put back. The sweep is split into four CLs by
directory to keep each one reviewable and cheap to revert.

#ai-assisted

parent
8fa61d044ce03ca1fb9305b29cd2a67e146f4377 [ diff ] 
Paint timing: attribute anonymous content-image pseudos via GeneratingNode

An image generated by "content: url(...)" on a pseudo element is laid
out as an anonymous LayoutImage, whose GetNode() is null.
ImagePaintTimingDetector::RecordImage() resolved non-background images
via GetNode(), and the soft navigation paint attribution tracker skipped
anonymous image objects, so these images were never LCP/ICP candidates
nor attributed to a soft navigation.

Resolve them via LayoutObject::GeneratingNode(), as ElementTiming and
RecordImage() for background images already do. The record keeps keying
on the painting LayoutObject, so removing the anonymous image still
clears it. This also makes list-style-image markers, the other anonymous
LayoutImage, LCP/ICP candidates, matching ElementTiming.

Both changes are gated on the new PaintTimingContentImagePseudoElements
runtime flag (experimental). It replaces AllImagesPaintedSentToElementTiming,
so a single flag covers all paint timing clients.
PaintTimingVisualizer::RecordObject() also uses GeneratingNode(), so
anonymous objects get a dom_node_id in traces.

Tests: unit tests for the enabled, disabled, removal and list marker
cases; WPTs for hard-navigation LCP and for ICP with and without a
competing text node.

[PopupCreator] [Transit] Treat a hidden WebContents as "not displayed" in HtmlElement

HtmlElement's exit Condition asks the origin WebContents' DOM whether
the node still has bounds in the viewport. When a trip opens a new tab
in the same window, the opener's WebContents is hidden but stays laid
out, so the DOM keeps answering "displayed" and the Condition never
fulfills.

This is why PopupMultiwindowPTTest#testPopupDoesNotOpenIfInFullscreen,
whose popup falls back to a new tab on phones, fails on every run of
android-17-x64-fyi-rel:
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/test/chromium/ninja:%2F%2Fchrome%2Fandroid:chrome_public_test_apk%2Forg.chromium.chrome.browser.popups.PopupMultiwindowPTTest%23testPopupDoesNotOpenIfInFullscreen

A DOM node in a destroyed or non-VISIBLE WebContents is by definition
not displayed, so NotDisplayedCondition is now fulfilled in that case.
The symmetric ENTER-side change is considered out of scope.

[Contextual Tasks] Deflake TabPicker browser tests

ContextualTasksForcedDarkModeBrowserTest.TabPicker (~0.5% flake) and
ContextualTasksBrowserTest.TabPicker run tab_picker_test.js and flaked
on win-rel across unrelated CLs. Several Mocha cases failed per run,
always on the menu open state (e.g. "Toggles tab menu on trigger
click" found the menu already open), and the unbounded-disabled case
crashed on the assert in openTabMenu_().

1. tab-picker-app opens and closes its menu on pointerenter and
   pointerleave, and cr-action-menu focuses items on mouseover. The
   bot's real mouse cursor can rest over the test window, so Blink
   sends trusted hover events whenever the trigger or menu is laid out
   under it. These race with the synthetic events the tests dispatch.
2. A capture listener on window or document can't filter them:
   pointerenter and pointerleave are not composed, so they stop at the
   tab-picker-app shadow root.

Fix:
- Set pointer-events: none on <body> for the suite so the real cursor
  never hits the page. dispatchEvent() and click() still work, and
  :hover can no longer change computed styles either.

Verification:
- Repro: with a real XTEST pointer sweeping the Xvfb screen, the
  unfixed test failed 4/20 runs; with the fix it passed 40/40.
- Local: 20/20 consecutive passes per suite via tools/autotest.py
- Swarm: 50/50 passes per suite across 10 shards via
  tools/run-swarmed.py (0 failures)

[PopupCreator] Keep the primary incognito profile alive for popup CCTs

When a popup is finishing but not yet destroyed, its IncognitoTabHost
reports no incognito tabs (hasIncognitoTabs() == false) while keeping
isActiveModel() == true. Because IncognitoStartup.onResumeWithNative()
only checked doIncognitoTabsExist(), a resuming ChromeTabbedActivity
could destroy the shared profile while the popup was still tearing down,
triggering an assertion in the popup'sTabModelSelectorProfileSupplier.

This caused PopupMultiwindowPTTest#testBasicIncognito to flake.

To fix this:
 - Update IncognitoStartup to also check !isIncognitoTabModelActive() before destroying the profile (matching IncognitoProfileDestroyer).
 - Register the popup's IncognitoTabHost in CustomTabIncognitoManager's ctor so the profile is held prior to native initialization.
 - Update FreshCtaTransitTestRule to finish and await destruction of non-tabbed activities before closing tabbed windows, and explicitly finish the popup in testBasicIncognito.

Flake verification:
https://chromium-swarm.appspot.com/task?id=7b5e47d645d6fa10

[PopupCreator] Re-enable the narrow launch-bounds popup tests on Brya

The desktop popup header is only drawn when the caption bar has room
for it, which is not the case in windows narrower than the OS caption
bar elements. PopupCreatorImpl always budgets for the header, so on
android-desktop-17-x64-rel-brya-tests the viewport of such popups came
out taller than requested.

testPopupOpensWithLaunchBounds_osWindowSizeLimit2 now opens a popup at
the minimum user-resizable width (386dp) and is renamed accordingly.
testPopupResizesOnWindowResizeBy asserts the outer window size, which
is what resizeBy() changes.

Flake verification: https://chromeos-swarming.appspot.com/task?id=7b752811faecc610

[PopupCreator] Predict popup window bounds by adding deltas to the viewport

getPopupInsetsForecast() expressed the difference between the requested
viewport bounds and the popup window bounds as negative Insets, which
createPopupActivityOptions() then subtracted from the viewport bounds.
Replace it with predictPopupWindowBounds(), which adds the delta width
and delta height to the requested viewport bounds and returns the
window bounds. No behavior change.

Fix hover flakes in OrganizerPanelTest.ListSectionItem

OrganizerListSectionItemElement uses MouseHoverableMixinLit to manage
hover state via the .hovered CSS class. However,
organizer_list_section_item.css also included raw :host(:hover) rules
for #actionButton and #trailingIcon.has-action-button.

On Windows bots, when the OS mouse cursor happens to be positioned over
the test element at (0, 0), :host(:hover) matches and native
pointerenter events can fire during microtasksFinished(), causing the
action button to be visible when the test expects the item to be
unhovered.

Remove the redundant :host(:hover) rules so hover visibility is
controlled consistently by .hovered and :focus-within, and explicitly
clear any initial .hovered class on the item and inner cr-url-list-item
before asserting unhovered state in the hover tests.

Test history:
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/test/chromium/%3A%2F%2Fchrome%2Ftest%5C%3Abrowser_tests%21gtest%3A%3AOrganizerPanelTest%23ListSectionItem

[ash] growth: get the active profile from the session

CampaignsManagerSession::GetProfile() used
ProfileManager::GetActiveUserProfile(), which is deprecated on ChromeOS
(crbug.com/40227502).

Resolve the active user's profile from the session instead: take the
account from SessionManager::GetActiveSession() and get its
BrowserContext via BrowserContextHelper. When there is no active session
this returns null, which the callers already handle. GetAccountId() also
reads the account from the active session.

Set the campaigns manager pref service and active account id from the
active User (GetProfilePrefs() and GetAccountId()) instead of resolving
a Profile, which removes that GetProfile() caller.

IsEligible() now checks the active User's conditions (is_managed() and
the guest user type) instead of the Profile, so it no longer needs a
Profile. The remaining GetProfile() users (owner settings,
AppServiceProxy, system web apps) keep it; those services exclude the
sign-in profile.

The unit tests log in a real user session (regular, managed, or guest)
so they exercise the session resolution directly, and
SetProfileForTesting is removed.

omnibox: Don't reserve 30 matches in every AutocompleteResult

AutocompleteMatch is 1.6 kB, and AutocompleteResult always reserved
30 of them, 50 kB.

Every AutocompleteController has two AutocompleteResults, and every
desktop window has two of these AutocompleteControllers (one for
the location bar, one for WebUI AI-mode composebox), for four
AutocompleteResults.

There's a fifth AutocompleteResult snapshot in SearchboxHandler.

Instead of unconditionally reserving this in every controller, do
it lazily when needed.

This saves 250 kB per window. Even after typing into the omnibox,
only used controllers will allocate.

For ten windows, this is a 2.5 MB memory reduction. (I currently have
70 Windows open.)

For one window, even after typing, this reduces memory use from 780 KB
(more allocations during typing) to 224 KB.

No intended behavior change

[ContextualTasks] Unselect restored session tabs

Unselecting a submitted or AIM-restored tab in the Contextual Tasks
extension tab picker previously left the tab selected on the first click
because `DeleteTabContext` only searched active attachments, while
extension context updates re-emitted deselected entries and left session
IDs without explicit tab-handle mappings unresolved. Re-selecting a
previously unselected tab also failed to clear deselection when
`CaptureAndUploadTabContext` passed a `TabHandle` value instead of the
tab's `SessionID`.

Delegate tab context deletion by `SessionID` to the session handle, skip
deselected tabs while resolving open tab handles when syncing context to
the extension page, and gate deselection checks consistently across
composebox and Contextual Tasks rearchitecture flags.

WebGLOnWebGPU: Load ANGLE_explicit_context entry points.

These allow for multiple interleaved contexts to be used in the
WebGLOnWebGPU layering.

To limit the binary size, the ContextANGLE functions are loaded in a
single loop, reusing the existing "glFoo" name literals with the
"ContextANGLE" suffix appended at runtime. They are stored as
contiguous fields at the end of ProcsGL, checked by static_asserts.

Based on https://crrev.com/c/8003602 by geofflang@.

[Indigo] Keep image edges blurred during the transformation animation

The blur layer was 3x the size of the image, so its backdrop-filter also
sampled pixels outside the image. Near the edges the unblurred image
showed through, more so as the blur increased (e.g. a face at the top
edge stayed sharp). This CL keeps the blur layer the size of the frame
and draws the sweep with its mask instead of moving the layer. The mask
is painted by a CSS paint worklet driven by a registered custom
property, so the sweep still animates on the compositor thread. The blur
strength now fades in through a second fixed-blur layer instead of
animating the blur radius, which avoids a visible jump near the peak.

parent
3b4eebb1f59fd2a6094b9001c9d35aa16d6c1c9e [ diff ] 
WebGLOnWebGPU: Give each context its own EGLDisplay.

ANGLE caches the displays returned by eglGetPlatformDisplay by their
attributes. The per-context Dawn proc table and wgpu::Instance aren't
part of this cache key, so a new WebGL context got the EGLDisplay of a
previous one, still alive, with its wgpu::Device. That device belongs to
the previous context's Dawn wire client: using it with the new
context's client hit the forClient == mClient assertion in Dawn.

Set EGL_PLATFORM_ANGLE_DISPLAY_KEY_ANGLE to the context address, so
that each context gets its own EGLDisplay.

Extracted from https://crrev.com/c/8003603 by geofflang@.

ChromeVox MV3: Replace panel caption in one step on flushed speech

When PrimaryTts speaks an utterance with QueueMode.FLUSH,
CATEGORY_FLUSH, or INTERJECT, it previously sent CLEAR_SPEECH
immediately and then ADD_NORMAL_SPEECH or ADD_ANNOTATION_SPEECH when the
utterance began speaking. Because PanelCommand.send() dispatches across
BridgeHelper asynchronously in MV3, those two commands arrived in
separate tasks and mutated #speech.innerHTML twice per flushed
utterance, letting a BeginMainFrame paint #speech empty between them and
invalidating the full panel width.

Defer clearing via clearSpeechPending_ in PrimaryTts.speakUsingQueue_()
and send a single SET_SPEECH command when
startSpeakingNextItemInQueue_() immediately speaks the next utterance.
If startSpeakingNextItemInQueue_() returns without speaking (such as
when currentVoice is still initializing, a delayed hint timer is
scheduled, or a doNotInterrupt utterance is still active), fall back to
sending CLEAR_SPEECH at the end of speakUsingQueue_() so stale captions
are never left on screen. PrimaryTts.stop() continues to send
CLEAR_SPEECH immediately.

Verified on nami/syndra with tast.ui.DocsCUJ.chromevox (6 interleaved
runs): Compositing.DirectRenderer.PartialSwap.ExtraDamage mean dropped
from 25.08% to 20.73% (median from 26.77% to 20.82%), restoring the
pre-MV3 baseline.

[Contextual Tasks] Extract ephemeral button context menu model

Moves the contextual tasks ephemeral toolbar button context menu out of
ContextualTasksButton into the new
ContextualTasksEphemeralButtonMenuModel, a ui::SimpleMenuModel that is
its own delegate, so that the upcoming WebUI toolbar implementation of
the button can show the same menu instead of duplicating it. This
follows the same pattern as SplitTabMenuModel, which the Views and WebUI
split tabs buttons share.

The model owns the PinnedActionToolbarButtonMenuModel and contains the
menu items (remove the button for the current task or close the side
panel, then pin, unpin and customize toolbar), their enabled and visible
state, and their command handling, including the RemoveByContextMenu
metrics. ContextualTasksButton now just creates the model and is no
longer a ui::SimpleMenuModel::Delegate. The remove item element
identifier moves to the model.

No behavior change intended.

[ContextualTasks] Fix Lens chip pixel tests

`ContextualTasksLensChipPixelTest` previously stretched a 1x1 green
pixel across a 200x60 frame, left `#closeButton` hidden in all four
variants so RTL screenshots duplicated LTR screenshots, and flaked
because `SetUpOnMainThread()` unconditionally re-added the built-in
component extension (reloading its service worker mid-test) and bound
`InputStateModel` before host navigation committed.

Remove the duplicate manual extension load since `ComponentLoader`
already installs the allowlisted extension at startup, attach the task
session after host navigation commits, and re-enable the suite to
capture a 52x52 chip with a synthetic crop preview across light/dark
surfaces and the focused dismiss scrim after polling decoded image,
layout, and computed style state and flushing the OOPIF compositor.

Agents: Add skill for authoring Chromium pixel tests

Adding a pixel test involves several manual steps that are easy to get
wrong and fail silently: the Screenshot step needs an
incompatible-action guard or it fails on non-pixel jobs; the test must
be registered in testing/buildbot/filters/pixel_tests.filter or it never
compares a pixel (several suites in the tree are in that state today);
and baseline_cl must be set to the CL's own number after the first
upload, which requires a second upload.

Add a pixel-test agent skill under //agents/skills/pixel-test/ that
automates the delegable steps and stops at the human ones:
 1. Decide whether the surface is deterministic enough to pixel-test.

2. Write the capture (Kombucha Screenshot/ ScreenshotSurface/
ScreenshotWebUi with SetOnIncompatibleAction, or DialogBrowserTest
set_baseline).

3. Register the test in pixel_tests.filter and verify the pattern
matches by running through the test launcher with
--test-launcher-filter-file (--gtest_list_tests bypasses the launcher
and ignores the filter).

4. Capture locally with --bypass-skia-gold-functionality and
   --skia-gold-local-png-write-directory and inspect the PNG.

5. Perform the baseline_cl two-upload sequence.

6. Hand off to the developer for Skia Gold triage, noting that tryjobs
   currently run pixel jobs with --bypass-skia-gold-functionality
   (crbug.com/574560342) so goldens are first produced post-submit.

The skill points at docs/testing/pixel_tests.md and the relevant headers
as sources of truth rather than restating APIs.

[ash] Forward-declare Profile, drop profile.h (1/4: ash UI)

Eleven files in chrome/browser/ui/ash and chrome/browser/ui/webui/ash
include chrome/browser/profiles/profile.h but only ever use Profile as
an opaque pointer: they name it in a signature, or store it in a member,
and pass it along without ever dereferencing it. A forward declaration
is enough, and in each case one is already reachable without this
include.

This is a class the earlier dead-include sweeps could not see. They
asked whether a file names Profile at all, and these files do, so they
were never candidates.

The candidates were picked per directory rather than tree-wide: these
are the directories where every profile.h includer qualifies, so the
chrome/browser/profiles dependency goes away instead of moving to a
sibling file. Three DEPS allowances and three build deps go with them,
in ui/ash/management_disclosure, ui/ash/read_write_cards,
ui/webui/ash/settings/pages/languages and
ui/webui/ash/settings/pages/search.

settings/pages/search keeps its DEPS allowance for now:
search_section_unittest.cc still includes profile.h without naming it,
and that include goes away with the reland of the dead-include sweep,
not here.

The compiler decided the rest: candidates were removed wholesale, then
chrome, unit_tests, browser_tests and interactive_ui_tests were built,
and everything it rejected was put back -- nearly all of those passing a
Profile* to a content::BrowserContext* parameter, an upcast that needs
the complete type. The sweep is split into four CLs by directory to keep
each one reviewable and cheap to revert.

#ai-assisted

[ash] auth: read prefs from the User, not a BrowserContext

Follow-up to post-submit review on https://crrev.com/c/8617961, which
replaced a Profile lookup with BrowserContextHelper plus
user_prefs::UserPrefs::Get(). Resolving a BrowserContext only to reach a
PrefService is not what ChromeOS code should do: user_manager::User
exposes that user's prefs directly through GetProfilePrefs(), which is
null in the same situations the BrowserContext lookup was -- the user's
profile is not ready yet, or is already gone.

The two "is this the primary user" tests become questions about the
session, since "primary" is a property of the session rather than of the
user: the primary session's account id is compared against the one being
asked about. SessionManager and its primary session are both absent
before log-in, which reads as "not primary", as it did before.

With the last BrowserContext gone the directory drops three build deps,
browser_context_helper, user_prefs and content/public/browser, and gains
session_manager/core.

[browser_actuator] Accept string_view in TransportSession::OnMessage

TransportSession::OnMessage only accepted a parsed MessageLite
reference, forcing FCM wake callers to deserialize each payload proto
just for TransportSessionImpl::OnMessage to re-serialize it, and leaving
dispatching_sequence_number_ unset on synchronous control replies.

Add TransportSession::OnMessage(PayloadType, std::string_view) to
dispatch serialized payload bytes directly and set
dispatching_sequence_number_ = 0 while dispatching so StartSessionAck
populates responding_to_sequence_number = 0. Delegate the existing
MessageLite overload to the string_view overload while callers migrate.

[Tab Capture] Respect incognito access in tabCapture.getMediaStreamId()

TabCaptureGetMediaStreamIdFunction previously passed a hardcoded true
for include_incognito when resolving target_tab_id and consumer_tab_id
via ExtensionTabUtil::GetTabById(). This allowed the regular context of
a split-mode extension to obtain a media stream ID for an incognito tab
(or designate an incognito consumer tab), unlike the fallback path,
tabCapture.capture(), and the tabs API.

Pass include_incognito_information() for both lookups so tab resolution
respects the calling extension context's incognito configuration, and
add browser tests covering split-mode and spanning-mode profile
boundaries.

Fix timeout flake in ChromeDelayLoadHookTest.ObserveDelayLoadFailure

EchoService::DelayLoad() intentionally triggers a fatal delay-load
failure (NOTREACHED / ImmediateCrash) inside the utility process. On
Windows builds with in-process stack dumping enabled, DbgHelp lazily
loads and parses browser_tests.exe.pdb inside the crashing utility
process to symbolize the stack trace, which frequently exceeds the 45s
test timeout under bot disk I/O contention.

Call base::debug::DisableInProcessStackDumpingForTesting() in
EchoService::DelayLoad(), matching EchoService::Crash() right above it.

Test history:
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/test/chromium/%3A%2F%2Fchrome%2Ftest%5C%3Abrowser_tests%21gtest%3A%3AChromeDelayLoadHookTest%23ObserveDelayLoadFailure

[Autofill] Log Autocomplete filling acceptance by field type.

Autocomplete currently records overall filling acceptance in
Autocomplete.KeyMetrics.FillingAcceptance, but does not break acceptance
down by the Autofill predicted field type. Measuring autocomplete
acceptance per field type helps evaluate the impact of excluding
sensitive ID types (such as passport, driver's license, and national ID
numbers) from Autocomplete.

Pass the validated FormStructure on form submission to
AutocompleteKeyMetricsLogger::OnFormSubmitted and record
Autocomplete.KeyMetrics.FillingAcceptance.ByFieldType for each predicted
FieldType of fields where autocomplete suggestions were shown.

Implement HfsForkReadStream in Rust DMG parser

Port HFSPlusExtentDescriptor, HFSPlusForkData, and HFSForkReadStream to
Rust in chrome/utility/safe_browsing/mac/rust/hfs.rs as part of the
macOS DMG parser Rustification effort:

- Add big-endian parsing for HfsPlusExtentDescriptor (8 bytes) and HfsPlusForkData (80 bytes, 8 inline extents).
- Implement HfsForkReadStream with std::io::Read and std::io::Seek across the 8 inline extents, enforcing the 64 MiB MAX_EXTENT_BUFFER_SIZE cap and checked arithmetic for block-to-byte offset calculations.
- Track intra-extent offsets explicitly across both Read and Seek so multi-extent reads advance and seek accurately while reusing cached extent data when staying within the loaded extent.
- Verify in SharedStream::read_at and SharedStream::read_exact_at that the underlying stream actually reached the requested offset before reading (matching HFSIterator::SeekToBlock behavior on streams that clamp out-of-bounds seeks).
- Add unit tests in dmg_parser_unittests.rs covering big-endian struct parsing, reading and seeking across all 8 extents, zero-length and sparse forks, oversized extent rejection, and out-of-bounds seeks.

gardener: Deflake two SettingsTest cases due to new foreground tabs

The test cases opened new foreground tabs, unintentionally putting the
tab under test to the background. This leads to throttling of the
Javascript execution, causing test timeouts.

This resolves two flaky tests:

* `SettingsComposePageTest.ComposePage`

While the failures of the first test case were observed during
gardening, the second identical scenario was identified by Jetski.

https://crrev.com/c/8624352 into a dedicated

COMMON_METADATA routing.

  and chrome/browser/) now also require content_patterns for the Sync
  APIs they cover.

  rule discovery.

  Sync-related C++ files under components/ (instead of all of them)

  renamed to check-is-tracking-metadata-before-getting-remote-specifics.

  a CHECK crash, and entity_tracker_ is wrapped in backticks so the file
  passes the markdown format presubmit.

[OptimizationGuide] Re-enable feature registry unit tests on iOS

MqlsFeatureRegistryTest.RegisterFeature and
SettingsUiRegistryTest.Register were disabled on iOS as flaky in
crrev.com/c/6908110 and crrev.com/c/6975069.

They were flaky because, at the time, the tests registered a mock
"Test" feature in the global MqlsFeatureRegistry / SettingsUiRegistry
singletons and cleared those singletons in TearDown(). Depending on the
order in which components_unittests ran in the same process, Register()
hit its duplicate-registration CHECK when production features had
already been registered, or later tests crashed on metadata that had
been cleared. crrev.com/c/7981542 fixed this root cause by giving both
fixtures an isolated local registry instance, so the iOS-only DISABLED_
guards are now obsolete.

Verified on an iPhone 17 (iOS 26.4) and an iPad Air 11-inch (M4)
(iOS 26.4) simulator: both tests pass 11/11 runs with --gtest_shuffle
together with the other tests of these files. No new test is added
since this CL only re-enables existing coverage.

[Test] Register gtest install_apk exceptions and re-raise BaseError

When https://crrev.com/c/6001353 updated Android test runners to
register InstallationError wrappers while re-raising the underlying
devil BaseError, the gtest install_apk path was left raising
TestException subclasses directly. Because TestException does not
inherit from BaseError, device failures during gtest APK installation
bypassed shard failure handling and exited with 1 instead of denylisting
the device with infra exit code 87. Registering the wrapper and
re-raising the original error aligns gtest setup with instrumentation
setup so broken devices are properly denylisted.

[mac] Initialize user data dir before InitMacCrashReporter

In ChromeMainDelegate::PreSandboxStartup(), InitMacCrashReporter() and
SetUpInstallerPreferences() were called before InitializeUserDataDir()
on macOS (unlike Linux/ChromeOS/Android, where InitializeCrashpad() runs
after InitializeUserDataDir()).

Because InitMacCrashReporter() calls crash_reporter::InitializeCrashpad(),
which queries ChromeCrashReporterClient::GetCrashMetricsLocation() and
ChromeCrashReporterClient::GetCollectStatsConsent() (both of which
resolve chrome::DIR_USER_DATA via base::PathService), calling
InitMacCrashReporter() before InitializeUserDataDir() caused PathService
to resolve and cache the default ~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome
directory even when --user-data-dir was explicitly passed on the command
line. On macOS 27 bots where the default directory could not be created,
this caused a fatal startup crash after crrev.com/c/7664504.

Initialize chrome::DIR_USER_DATA via InitializeUserDataDir() before
calling InitMacCrashReporter() and SetUpInstallerPreferences() on macOS.

[DBSC] Add AI code review skill and rules for net/device_bound_sessions

Adds DBSC-specific guidance for the Chromium AI code reviewer in two
parts:

- agents/skills/device-bound-sessions-review/SKILL.md: the DBSC
  architecture and privacy model (including the prewarming exception),
  the standalone, SSO and federated registration flows, judgment calls
  that reviewers make on DBSC CLs (behavior and error-order changes,
  layering, metrics, persistence), how to flag drift between the code
  and this guidance, and known false positives.
- 15 knowledge-base rules under net/device_bound_sessions/knowledge_base/,
  one invariant each: exactly-once async completion, revalidating
  sessions after re-entrant calls and async steps, SessionError and
  RefreshResult semantics, validating server-supplied origins, fetch
  setup and redirects, failure sentinels, JWT construction, feature
  flags for web-visible changes, scoping request-path histograms, the
  pre-provisioned key lifecycle, side-effect-free SessionStore reads,
  priority inversion in key restore, transient errors, spec
  conformance, and tests that fail without the change.

The guidance comes from recurring review feedback on about 290 merged
DBSC CLs.

net/device_bound_sessions/DIR_METADATA lists the skill in one
agentic_review capability group and all rules in another, so every rule
loads for any .cc, .h or .proto change under this directory.

[Contextual Tasks] Extract UI-agnostic ephemeral button logic

Moves the contextual tasks ephemeral toolbar button logic that does
not depend on Views out of ContextualTasksButton into the new
contextual_tasks_ephemeral_button_utils.{h,cc}, so that the upcoming
WebUI toolbar implementation of the button can share it instead of
duplicating it. The shared helpers cover:
- side panel alignment, and the button shape and dock position derived
  from it (leading edge, before the profile button, or trailing edge)
- whether the button should be shown
- press handling: toggling the side panel and recording its metrics
- the Shown metric

ToolbarView now uses the shared ShouldPlaceCircularButtonBeforeProfile()
and IsEphemeralButtonTrailing() helpers instead of re-deriving them,
so ContextualTasksButton::IsSidePanelRightAligned() and IsTrailing()
are removed.

No behavior change intended.

dacd09f9c2c0750d69c8295b6ede92457708e103 [ diff ] 
[sync] Make CryptographerImpl key-emplacing select default

Previously, CryptographerImpl::EmplaceKey() and
CryptographerImpl::EmplaceAllNigoriKeysFrom() added keys to the keybag
without updating the default encryption key, requiring every production
caller to immediately follow up with a separate call to
SelectDefaultEncryptionKey().

This patch replaces EmplaceKey() with RotateDefaultKeyByDerivation(),
which atomically derives the key, adds it to the keybag, and selects it
as the default encryption key. Similarly, callers of
EmplaceAllNigoriKeysFrom() now use TryFollowRemoteKeyRotation() directly
with KeystoreKeysCryptographer::GetKeystoreKeybag() and
GetLastKeystoreKeyName() (replacing ToCryptographerImpl() and avoiding a
temporary CryptographerImpl).

With all public key-mutating operations now atomically selecting a
default encryption key, EmplaceKeysFrom() and
SelectDefaultEncryptionKey() are made private and CryptographerImpl
enforces the invariant that default_encryption_key_name_ is empty iff
key_bag_ is empty.

Reland "[ash] Drop dead profile.h includes" (1/4: ash UI)

This is a reland of commit 499ae8c51418fbcc82eb1465ed67061837c71c97,
split into four CLs by directory. This part covers chrome/browser/ui/ash
and chrome/browser/ui/webui/ash: 31 includes across 33 files. Two DEPS
allowances go away, in ui/ash/boca and
ui/webui/ash/settings/pages/printing/integration_tests, which had no
other user of chrome/browser/profiles.

These files include chrome/browser/profiles/profile.h but never name
Profile: the include survived whatever once used it. Candidates were
removed wholesale, then chrome, unit_tests, browser_tests and
interactive_ui_tests were built, and everything the compiler rejected
was put back.

The original was reverted over two scanning crosier tests that use
Profile without ever spelling it. They sit in a crosier_tests target
under is_chromeos_device, which none of those four targets build, so the
compiler never saw them. They keep their include and appear in none of
the four parts.

[mac] Hide the views compositor when the window is occluded

When a browser window is occluded, currently viz is not notified, which
prevents it from releasing buffers. This has previously been addressed
for minimized windows and space transitions, but not for occlusion,
which is done (under a new flag) in this CL.

This is based on WebContentsOcclusionCheckerMac's occlusion state, with
an important change vs WebContents occlusion: debouncing (to prevent
churn when quickly (dis)occluded) is set to 1.5s, vs 1s elsewhere. This
is intentional to pause after renderers stop producing frames, reducing
the likelihood of retained tiles. No other mechanism enforces the
ordering as it's not a correctness issue.

Not gated by the flag: WebContentsOcclusionCheckerMac now clears a
window's occluded state when its last WebContents is removed (so it
cannot get stuck), and forwards occlusion updates to
NativeWidgetMacNSWindowHost (which ignores them when the flag is off).

Note that the current state of the code is not idea: there is a layer
inversion, tracking should be in components/remote_cocoa, not contents.
This would be consistent with aura, but addressing it is out of scope
for this CL.

JNI Zero: Name the receiving method in pointer leaks

When generated glue passes a JniRawPtr or JniUniquePtr to a
@CalledByNative method, it now also passes a description of the
receiver, e.g. "passed to org.chromium.foo.Foo#bar parameter ptr", and
LifetimeAssert appends it to its failure message. The description is
only passed when DCHECKs are on.

SuperSize: Speed up CalculatePadding()

This loop runs over every symbol when loading a non-sparse .size file.
* Iterate with zip() rather than copying the list and indexing.
* Inline IsOverhead(), IsNative() and end_address.
* Check IsNative() only for the current symbol, since the previous
  symbol is known to be in the same section at that point.

Expected speed-up: CalculatePadding() for one ~2.1M-symbol .size file:
1.14s -> 0.46s (identical results). ~1.4s for
create_patched_supersize_diff.py, which loads two such files [E].

Parameterize degraded recoverability metrics by SecurityDomainId

Degraded recoverability metrics in TrustedVault
(RecoverabilityStatusOnRequestCompletion,
TrustedVaultDegradedRecoverabilityValue, and
TrustedVaultHintDegradedRecoverabilityChangedReason) were previously
recorded into unpartitioned histograms across Chrome Sync and Passkeys
security domains. Which caused the blending of metrics from different
security domains.

This CL parameterizes the corresponding histograms with the
SecurityDomainId, and updates unit tests.

SuperSize: Speed up parsing of .size files

In _LoadSizeInfoFromFile():
* Parse numeric lines with map(int) and itertools.accumulate() rather
  than a per-value Python loop.
* Fast-path symbol lines that have no aliases or flags (no tab), and
  parse aliases / flags directly rather than via intermediate strings.
* Hoist models.Symbol.__new__ and STRING_LITERAL_NAME out of the loop.

Expected speed-up: LoadSizeInfo() for one ~2.1M-symbol .size file:
4.91s -> 4.26s (identical results). ~1.4s for
create_patched_supersize_diff.py, which loads two such files [E].

SuperSize: Disable cyclic GC while loading in supersize console

Loading .size files creates millions of long-lived Symbol objects,
which causes Python's cyclic GC to repeatedly scan the full heap.
* --query runs exit via os._exit(0), so GC is left disabled.
* Interactive sessions re-enable GC after loading, but first call
  gc.freeze() so that loaded objects are excluded from collections.

Also fixes a typo in a comment.

Expected speed-up: create_patched_supersize_diff.py (which uses
--query): 107.05s -> 90.44s (identical output) [E].

Remove checking for Ad-Auction-Only response header.

This would block responses with the Ad-Auction-Only header from being
sent to renderers (or anything else without a trusted URLLoaderFactory).
As Protected Audiences has been removed, this code is no longer needed.

It did provide some limited security to ensure renderers never received
responses intended for auction worklets, but given the feature now has
zero usage, and has been deprecated for quite some time, it should
be safe to remove this code.

rcaps: Remove IsInEeaCountry() from Android DSE NTP & Feed

Since `NewTabSearchEngineUrlAndroid` rolled out globally in
https://crrev.com/c/6821564,
`DseNewTabUrlManager.isNewTabSearchEngineUrlAndroidEnabled()`,
`FeedSurfaceMediator`, and `FeedFeatures.isFeedEnabledByDSE()` apply in
all regions on Android. However, two `IsInEeaCountry()` call sites were
left behind:
- `DseNewTabUrlManager` still wrote
  `mRegionalCapabilities.isInEeaCountry()` to
  `ChromePreferenceKeys.IS_EEA_CHOICE_COUNTRY`, which is no longer read
  anywhere in production.
- `FeedServiceFactory` still set
  `chrome_info.is_new_tab_search_engine_url_android_enabled` to
  `regional_capabilities->IsInEeaCountry()`, leaving
  `FeedStream::IsFeedEnabledByDse()` out of sync with the Java Feed
  layer outside the EEA.

Key changes:
- Removes `mRegionalCapabilities` and `IS_EEA_CHOICE_COUNTRY` from
  `DseNewTabUrlManager`, deprecating
  `"Chrome.SearchEngine.IsEeaChoiceCountry"`.
- Removes `ChromeInfo::is_new_tab_search_engine_url_android_enabled` and
  `RegionalCapabilitiesService` from `FeedServiceFactory`, so
  `FeedStream::IsFeedEnabledByDse()` unconditionally checks
  `snippets_enabled_by_dse_` on Android.

[Enterprise] Support computer_name CN in Browser and Profile delegates

Allow ManagedClientCertificateForBrowserConfig and
ManagedClientCertificateForUserConfig to configure client certificates
to use the sanitized device hostname as the Subject Common Name (CN):
- Read "common_name_source" from the companion config policy prefs in
  BrowserContextDelegate and ProfileContextDelegate when
  kClientCertCommonNameAttribute is enabled.
- Fall back to the default Client ID / Profile ID if the config policy
  is not set to "computer_name" or if the sanitized device hostname is
  empty.

[Android] Speed up browsertest post-test teardown

Start Activity teardown at the beginning of
AndroidBrowserTest::PostRunTestOnMainThread() and disallow undo in
TabModelJniBridge.forceCloseAllTabs() so closing all tabs does not
inflate HubLayout tab-switcher or undo snackbar UI right before
destroying the Activity. Also hide ChromeBrowserTestsActivity's
DecorView and disable screenshots/close animations on teardown, and
skip ShardEnder's process-death polling loop when no shards remain.

Measured with Perfetto traces of `AndroidBrowserTest.Smoke` on x86_64
Android Desktop (`android-desktop-x64-rel` GN args, uncompiled
`run-from-apk` mode matching CQ shards):
- Post-test teardown (Perfetto): 224 ms -> 118 ms (-106 ms / -47%)
- Per-test `am instrument` wall time: 1,116 ms -> 1,023 ms (-94 ms / -8.4%)
- Estimated CQ savings across `android_browsertests` (5,655 tests):
  ~8.9 min total bot time per `android-desktop-x64-rel` build (~11s/shard
  across 50 shards; ~45s/shard on 12-shard Android builders).

[PA] Batch SchedulerLoopQuarantine stats updates

Every quarantined entry did 4 atomic read-modify-write operations on
the SchedulerLoopQuarantineRoot stats, and every purge 2 more. These
atomics are shared by all the branches of a root (i.e. by all threads),
so they are both slow on their own and prone to cache line contention.

In the Windows Stable congestion (jank) profile of the browser main
thread, 1.95% of samples are in Quarantine(), where these updates are
inlined:
http://pprof/?id=6f6060560ac44f3cec78b4b91c2176c3&pivot=partition_alloc::internal::SchedulerLoopQuarantineBranch%3C1,0%3E::Quarantine

Accumulate the stats in the branch instead, and publish them to the
root every 64 quarantined entries and whenever the branch is fully
purged (e.g. at the end of a task). The only consumer of these stats is
the memory-infra dump provider, for which slightly lagging stats are
fine. Tests can force publication with PublishStatsForTesting().

This grows ThreadCache by 32 bytes, which fits thanks to the parent CL.

SchedulerLoopQuarantinePerfTest results on Pinpoint ("all lines" rows
read every cache line of each object before freeing it, like a
destructor that reads all fields):

Significance: ◆ p < 0.05, ◆◆ p < 0.01, ◆◆◆ p < 0.001

[clang/rust] Use git instead of gitiles wherever possible

`build.py`, `build_rust.py`, and `build_crubit.py` used Gitiles' REST
API (via `urllib`) to get the latest LLVM, Rust, and Crubit commits and
to read Rust's `src/stage0`. These requests are always anonymous, and
Git-on-Borg no longer covers anonymous traffic by its SLOs: it is the
first to be rejected under load.

This CL routes these requests through `git` instead:
- replaced the fetching latest commit hash logic with `git ls-remote`
- replaced the fetching on src/stage0 when packackging rust with
  `git fetch`

On LUCI builds, git rewrites `https://chromium.googlesource.com/` to the
authenticated `/a/` endpoint, during the `bot_update` step, So the same
queries to the LLVM, Rust, and Crubit repos should also be authenticated
by default using git CLIs

[ios blink] Fix blank pages when opening media URLs

Opening supported audio/video URLs directly shows a blank page on iOS
Blink instead of the media player.

Remove the outdated iOS exclusion from media MIME recognition so these
responses can render as media documents. Make Blink common's media
dependency unconditional; WebKit-based iOS Chrome does not link Blink
common.

some of the last suites to finish on mac-rel builds, and their shards
have 20+min runtimes, eg:

extra overheard incurred by this doesn't break the bank?

[test] Install only required System Web Apps in FilesAppBrowserTest

FileManagerBrowserTestBase::StartTest() previously called
SystemWebAppManager::InstallSystemAppsForTesting(), which installs all
~24 default-enabled System Web Apps on ChromeOS (Camera, Diagnostics,
Print Management, Scanning, Crosh, Terminal, Help, Personalization,
Shortcut Customization, etc.) before every single FilesAppBrowserTest.

Each SWA installation goes through ExternallyManagedAppManager, creates
WebAppInstallInfo, runs icon checks, and registers with AppService. Only
4 SWAs are actually used across the FilesAppBrowserTest suite:
- FILE_MANAGER (the Files app under test)
- MEDIA (Gallery/Backlight, used by OpenAudioMediaApp /
  OpenVideoMediaApp / OpenImageMediaApp tests)
- SETTINGS (OS Settings, used by SkyVault / ManageMirroredFolders tests)
- OS_FEEDBACK (used by DefakeSendFeedback tests)

Add an overload of SystemWebAppManager::InstallSystemAppsForTesting()
that accepts a flat_set<SystemWebAppType> and filters
`system_app_delegates_` before installing, and use it in
FileManagerBrowserTestBase::StartTest() to install only those 4 SWAs.

[test] Run VideoCaptureService in-process in fast test builds

On every `browser_tests` and `interactive_ui_tests` startup, the browser
spawns a dedicated utility process for
`video_capture.mojom.VideoCaptureService` (triggered by Ash Privacy Hub
`CameraPresenceNotifier` or `MediaDevicesManager`).

When `EXPENSIVE_TEST_LOGIC_IS_ON()` is false, enable
`features::kRunVideoCaptureServiceInBrowserProcess` in
`InProcessBrowserTest::Initialize()` (excluded on macOS where the
service requires a `CFRunLoop`, https://crbug.com/40572495).

Expected cost savings: ~3.5-5% reduction in `browser_tests` total CPU
time (~150-225 ms CPU saved per test) and ~25-35 bot-minutes per
`linux-chromeos-rel` CQ build.

Android: Relax signflinger CPU feature check to match new binary

signflinger's native-image is now built with
-march=x86-64-v2 -H:CPUFeatures=AVX,AVX2,BMI2,SHA,CLMUL,AES rather than
-march=x86-64-v3 -H:CPUFeatures=SHA,CLMUL,AES. Update the /proc/cpuinfo
check so that hosts lacking LZCNT, BMI1, FMA, F16C or MOVBE can still
use the native binary.

[iOS] Deflake and re-enable BackgroundRefreshAppAgentTest.ExpireTask

This CL fixes flakiness in BackgroundRefreshAppAgentTest.ExpireTask and
re-enables the test.

ExpireTask failed flakily on simulator bots for three reasons:
1. BuildMockTask originally captured the expiration handler block into a
   __weak variable via -[NSInvocation getArgument:atIndex:], causing
   undefined behavior under ARC (subsequently fixed by
   crrev.com/c/6554264 and crrev.com/c/6979688).
2. InvokeTaskHandlerThen chained thenCallback directly on
   scheduler_callback_runner_ instead of posting it to the UI thread
   after -systemTriggeredExecutionForTask: enqueued
   -handleExecutionForTask:, allowing run_loop_.Run() to return before
   the main-thread execution handler started the provider.
3. ProlongedTask used a hardcoded sleep(1) on a background ThreadPool
   thread before setting executed = YES. Under simulator CPU contention,
   the 1-second sleep could finish before task expiration or before the
   test verified that executed was FALSE.

To make task expiration deterministic, ProlongedTask now waits on a
base::WaitableEvent that is signaled when TestRefreshProvider cancels
the refresh, and InvokeTaskHandlerThen hops thenCallback to the UI
thread via base::BindPostTask(web::GetUIThreadTaskRunner({}), ...).

Re-enables BackgroundRefreshAppAgentTest.ExpireTask.

Fix flake in UpdateActiveTabContextStatusOnTabSwitch test

UpdateActiveTabContextStatusOnTabSwitch registers
EXPECT_CALL(*mock_handler, UpdateSuggestedTabContext(testing::IsNull()))
with .WillOnce() before opening the side panel. However,
UpdateSuggestedTabContext(nullptr) can be invoked multiple times or
before the tab switch (e.g., from an asynchronous OnEligibilityChange
callback posted during tab setup or from
DelayedUpdateSuggestedTabContext), either prematurely quitting
tab_switch_run_loop or exceeding the .WillOnce() expectation.

Use .WillRepeatedly() gated on the tab switch step so
tab_switch_run_loop only quits after ActivateTab() is called.

Test history:
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/test/chromium/%3A%2F%2Fchrome%2Ftest%5C%3Ainteractive_ui_tests%21gtest%3A%3AContextualTasksSidePanelCoordinatorInteractiveUiTest%23UpdateActiveTabContextStatusOnTabSwitch

[iOS] Re-enable URLOpenerParamsTest.initWithUIOpenURLContext on device

This CL re-enables URLOpenerParamsTest.initWithUIOpenURLContext on
physical devices.

`UIOpenURLContext` and `UISceneOpenURLOptions` cannot be instantiated
directly in tests because UIKit marks `+new` and `-init` as
`NS_UNAVAILABLE` and exposes only read-only properties, so they must be
mocked. The test was disabled on device in crrev.com/c/2669722 because
it used strict `[OCMockObject mockForClass:]` mocks, which fail whenever
UIKit or the runtime invokes unstubbed methods (such as `-description`
or internal UIKit methods on device). Switching to nice class mocks
(`OCMClassMock`) and typed `OCMStub` calls—matching
`TaskRequestForURLContextTest` (crrev.com/c/8140146)—ignores harmless
unstubbed calls while stubbing `URL` and `sourceApplication` for
`initWithUIOpenURLContext:`.

mojo: Remove Configuration::dont_advertise_capabilities

dont_advertise_capabilities stopped legacy Mojo Core's NodeChannel from
advertising its capabilities to its peer, so that tests could exercise
capability skew between client versions. mojo-ipcz has no such concept
and never reads the field.

Remove the field along with its test-only plumbing: the
disable-all-capabilities switch, which ScopedMojoSupport and
MultiprocessTestHelper each defined, and
MultiprocessTestHelper::LaunchType::CHILD_WITHOUT_CAPABILITIES, which
only made the child pass that switch. Its only user was the
MultiprocessMessagePipeTestWithPeerSupport instantiation, where it now
behaved exactly like LaunchType::CHILD, so no coverage is lost.

Dropping that test parameter renumbers the ones after it, so update the
iOS mojo_unittests filter to keep excluding the same CHILD and ASYNC
instances.

Also fix two stale #endif comments next to the touched code.

[omnibox][aim] Render suggestion activity link inside the popup card

The "Suggestions based on your Google activity" link in the AIM omnibox
popup was rendered as a sibling after #composebox. #composebox is the
visible card, so the link showed up in a separate strip hanging below
the card instead of as its last row (see the mock on b:517601900).

Move the link inside #composebox. The mic and submit buttons are
absolutely positioned against the bottom of #composebox, so lift them
by the link's height while the link is present to keep them aligned
with the context menu row. The grid layout anchors them to the top and
is left alone.

Also hide the link once the user starts typing. It explains
zero-suggest suggestions based on the user's activity, so it doesn't
apply to typed results.

Give the link the dimmed omnibox text color (the `unset` token made it
inherit the primary text color), drop the stale "No activity
suggestion disclaimer" comment, and remove two custom properties that
nothing reads.

[a11y-canvas] Collect accessibility UKM metrics for OffscreenCanvas placeholders

Record Accessibility.Canvas UKM metrics for OffscreenCanvas instances
associated with a DOM placeholder canvas element.

Previously, NeedsAccessibilitySupport, HasKeyboardListener, and
HasMouseListener were skipped when is_offscreen was true causing
missed listener UKM recording.

This CL resolves the associated placeholder HTMLCanvasElement:
- Standalone OffscreenCanvas instances without a DOM placeholder skip
  recording.
- On the main thread, the placeholder is inspected directly for
  visibility, keyboard/mouse listeners, and the accessibility
  heuristic. If the placeholder DOM node has been destroyed, infinite
  rescheduling loops are prevented, and if it is temporarily undisplayed,
  recording is deferred until displayed.
- On worker threads, a cross-thread task is dispatched to the main
  thread's compositor task runner using primitive value arguments
  (DOMNodeId, enum, bool) rather than object pointers, avoiding
  cross-thread Oilpan heap references or dangling pointers.
- Worker threads attempt recording at most once, immediately setting
  did_record_accessibility_ukm_ to true. This prevents fast
  worker animation loops from flooding the main thread task queue, and
  avoids complex cross-thread retry ping-pong since 5 seconds of draw
  time already allows the placeholder DOM element to be displayed.
- Unit tests use context->DidDraw() directly to record text and
  interaction draw operations, removing fillTextForTesting entirely
  from CanvasRenderingContext and CanvasRenderingContext2D.
- Adds RecordUKMCanvasAccessibilityForTesting() and
  CanvasAccessibilityUkmMetricsWorkerTest to verify offscreen canvas
  metric recording from dedicated worker threads.

base: call GetAppOutputWithExitCodeAndTimeout callback while waiting

crrev.com/c/7007597 stopped calling `still_waiting` on each wait
iteration, so a child that writes no output only gets one callback,
right after launch.

The Windows updater reads InstallerProgress from this callback, and
setup.exe writes no output, so the update progress in
chrome://settings/help stays at 50% for the whole install.

Move the PermissionPromptPreviewsCoordinator member and its lifecycle
helpers (MaybeAddMediaPreview and UpdateMediaDevicePreferenceRanking)

[gpu][webnn] Add WebNNScopedAccess for automatic SyncToken management

To support automatic SyncToken management (behind the
UseAutomaticSyncTokenManagement feature) for WebNN/WebGPU SharedImage
interop, this CL introduces gpu::WebNNScopedAccess and
ClientSharedImage::BeginWebNNAccess():

1. ClientSharedImage::BeginWebNNAccess() constructs a WebNNScopedAccess
and invokes the caller-provided callback with either SyncTokens
collected from the ClientSharedImage (in the automatic SyncToken mode)
or a single-element vector containing the passed-in SyncToken (in the
manual mode). The callback wraps CreateTensorFromMailbox() (in
MLContext::createExportableTensor()) or ImportTensor() (in
MLTensor::ExportToGPUImpl()).

2. WebNNScopedAccess::EndAccess() invokes the caller-provided callback
(wrapping ExportTensor() / ExportTensorSync() in
MLTensor::ExportToGPUImpl()) and stores its returned SyncToken in the
automatic mode.

3. As a supporting change, WebNNContext::CreateTensorFromMailbox(),
WebNNTensor::ImportTensor(), and GpuTaskScheduler::ScheduleGpuTask() are
updated to accept a vector of SyncTokens accordingly.

[Enterprise] Support custom CN in CertificateProvisioningService

When enterprise admins configure a custom Subject Common Name (CN)
source for managed client certificates, CertificateProvisioningService
needs to request certificates with that CN and renew existing
certificates if the configured CN changes.

- Pass the expected CN to KeyUploadClient::CreateCertificate() to
  populate BrowserPublicKeyUploadRequest::common_name when
  kClientCertCommonNameAttribute is enabled.
- Validate loaded certificates via
  ContextDelegate::ShouldCertificateBeRenewed() and observe the
  companion config policy pref so CN source changes trigger renewal.
- Support custom common_name in RequestHandlerForBrowserPublicKeyUpload
  for testing.

[EVP] Polish Android email verification loading UI

Address UX review feedback on the Android Email Verification Protocol
UI.

First-run bottom sheet:
- Use the "mark email read" icon instead of the generic email icon.
- Show the loading spinner inside the "Verify" button instead of below
  the buttons. The button keeps its size and color while loading; only
  its label is swapped for a spinner, and its content description is set
  to "Verifying email" for accessibility. Previously the button was
  disabled (greyed out) and a separate LoadingView was shown.

Subsequent-run loading Message:
- Follow Translate's loading pattern: keep a static icon on the left and
  show a non-clickable progress spinner in place of the primary action
  button. Previously the spinner replaced the icon and a "Cancel" button
  was shown. Swiping the message away still cancels the verification.
- Add MessageWrapper::SetPrimaryWidgetAppearance() so native features
  can use PrimaryWidgetAppearance::PROGRESS_SPINNER, and remove
  MessageWrapper::ShowLoadingSpinner(), which no longer has callers.

Reland "Reland "[Webium] Enable omnibox popup deferral in testing config""

This is a reland of commit 22b0dc5d078e1920c493f902c1e417d8214f31e8

The previous reland made
OmniboxAimPopupBrowserTest.ActivePermissionPromptPreventsPopupClose
crash on Mac13 Tests with NOTREACHED in
MockPermissionPromptFactory::DoNotCreate().

The test leaves a permission request pending on the AIM popup's
WebContents and owned its MockPermissionPromptFactory as a local. When
the local goes out of scope, the factory points the
PermissionRequestManager at DoNotCreate(), which must never run. The
manager shows its prompt again each time its WebContents turns visible.
With OmniboxAimPopupDeferCreation enabled, the Mac crash stack shows a
popup autoresize unhiding the content's NSView after the test body
returns, so the manager asks DoNotCreate() for a prompt.

This reland stores the factory in a fixture member, which outlives the
browser. A prompt recreated during teardown then comes from the live
factory, and once the manager is destroyed the factory stops serving it.

Mac13 Tests runs this test only in CI, so the footers below run it on
the mac13-tests try builder.

Original change's description:
> Reland "[Webium] Enable omnibox popup deferral in testing config"
>
> This is a reland of commit 957cf646363239c26e155c1e26262a22e23eb5c4
>
> The original change broke
> OmniboxAimPopupBrowserTest.CreatesContentWithPresenterWithoutDeferCreation
> on Linux Tests. That test covers the AIM popup without
> OmniboxAimPopupDeferCreation, the feature's default state, but never
> set the feature; it relied on the default. Browser tests apply
> fieldtrial_testing_config.json, so once the original change enabled the
> feature there, the test ran with deferral on and failed its first
> assertion, ASSERT_FALSE(IsEnabled(kOmniboxAimPopupDeferCreation)).
>
> The reland moves the test to OmniboxAimPopupNoDeferCreationBrowserTest,
> a fixture whose ScopedFeatureList disables the feature. A
> ScopedFeatureList override takes precedence over the testing config, so
> the test again exercises the non-deferred path regardless of the
> config. The deferred path stays covered by
> OmniboxAimPopupDeferCreationBrowserTest, which enables the feature the
> same way.
>
> Original change's description:
> > [Webium] Enable omnibox popup deferral in testing config
> >
> > WebUIReloadButtonStudy bundles startup work deferrals that keep a new
> > browser window's first frame off the critical path. The omnibox
> > suggestion popup and the AI Mode popup still create their WebUI
> > content, a WebContents and a navigation each, while the window is
> > built.
> >
> > OmniboxWebUIPopupDeferCreation and OmniboxAimPopupDeferCreation move
> > that creation after the window's first presentation. This enables both
> > in the study's testing config so that tests cover the configuration
> > the Canary and Dev Finch groups will run.
> >
> > Bug: b:567847083
> > Test: CQ dry run
> > Change-Id: Ib2a14c2356b1d5e1bf5b62de09c4cda46a6a6964
> > Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8629587

> > Commit-Queue: Fergal Daly <fergal@chromium.org>
> > Cr-Commit-Position: refs/heads/main@{#1724645}
>
> Bug: b:567847083
> Test: browser_tests --gtest_filter='OmniboxAimPopup*:OmniboxWebUIPopupDeferCreation*'
> Change-Id: I57a62abd1603b7d0f7ca23fcc15b9ccb9591f335
> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8630410

[ozone/x11] Apply multi-rectangle input regions

PlatformWindow::SetInputRegion() takes a list of rectangles, but the X11
implementation only applied the first one, and DCHECKed that the list
had exactly one entry. A release build silently truncates the region, so
callers that legitimately pass several rectangles (as the Wayland and
ChromeOS backends support) get the wrong hit-test area.

Union the rectangles into an SkRegion and send the resulting rectangles,
which are YXBanded-sorted by construction, mirroring
X11Window::SetShape(). A non-empty list whose rectangles are all
degenerate now resets the region, same as an empty list.

Add input-shape coverage to ui/ozone/platform/x11/test: a single
rectangle, multiple rectangles in unsorted order, overlapping
rectangles, and the reset path.

Update fake_dmserver desktop docs for domain signatures

fake_dmserver only includes pre-computed production signatures for
example.com, chromepolicytest.com, and managedchrome.com. Standard
desktop Chrome and Chromium validate policies against the compiled-in
production verification key. Setting use_universal_signing_keys uses
a test verification key that desktop builds reject.

Update desktop_instructions.md to document the supported domains and
clarify that use_universal_signing_keys is not for local desktop
testing.

Android: Explain how to lay out views in android-do-not-mock skill

Adds a "Laying out views" section to the android-do-not-mock skill.
Detached views are measured and laid out directly, while attached views
should be laid out by Robolectric's real ViewRootImpl pass
(RobolectricUtil.runAllBackgroundAndUi() after setContentView()). Also
covers sizing the window with @Config qualifiers without accidentally
switching to tablet resources, and calls out two anti-patterns: calling
layout() on an attached view's ancestors to simulate a layout pass, and
assuming an attached view sits at the window origin.

enable_reporting was disabled on all iOS builds, so the Reporting API
was compiled out of iOS Blink. This CL enables it on the iOS Blink port.

[WebApps/Android] Add async install-state query to WebappRegistry

The omnibox install button calls WebappRegistry.isAppInstalledForUrl()
on the UI thread. That method makes synchronous PackageManager IPC
calls, which causes ANRs under heavy load (crbug.com/568980174).

To prevent that from happening in the future, this CL creates 2
functions that will make hooking up to the install button simpler:
- An async API that runs in the background thread and posts tasks
  back on the UI thread (`queryIsAppInstalledForUrl()`).
- `getAppInstallStateKeyForUrl()`, which returns a cache key for the
  install state of a url. It reads only the registry's in-memory
  state and makes no IPC calls. The key has the url's origin, the
  number of verified TWA delegate apps for that origin, and the sorted
  package names of registered WebAPKs whose scope contains the url.
  It does not check that these apps are still installed. Callers can
  reuse a cached `queryIsAppInstalledForUrl()` result for urls with
  the same key. A registry change that can affect the result gives a
  new key.

This CL has no behavior change because the new methods have no callers
yet. A follow-up CL will connect ToolbarManager to this API.

[sync] Add CryptographerImpl::TryFollowRemoteKeyRotation

This patch introduces CryptographerImpl::TryFollowRemoteKeyRotation(),
which encapsulates remote keybag rotation and key continuity enforcement
directly inside CryptographerImpl.

NigoriSyncBridgeImpl::TryDecryptPendingKeysWith() now delegates remote
key rotation and key continuity verification to
TryFollowRemoteKeyRotation(), allowing the temporary
GetDefaultKeyNamePossiblyInvalidated() getter to be removed.

This is a reland of commit 7d062bcf5b86e6740d3d0414624363d34ef970a4.

Original change caused test failures on linux-arm64 bots because the
host protoc binary cannot execute on arm64 targets. This reland excludes

Original change's description:
> policy: Write report uploads from fake_dmserver as textproto
>

> chrome_profile_report upload to a human-readable .textproto file in the
> client state directory for debugging. fake_dmserver pipes the request
> body to `protoc --decode` on stdin, and writes stdout to the file. If
> the formatter fails, fake_dmserver logs an error and deletes the file.
>
> Linux desktop only.

Fix flake in PageLoadMetricsBrowserTest.InputEventsForFormSubmission

When InitialWebUI and WebUIReloadButton are enabled via
fieldtrial_testing_config.json on Windows, WebUIToolbarWebView loads
chrome://webui-toolbar.top-chrome in a background WebContents. If that
navigation commits or reloads while InputEventsForFormSubmission is
measuring Navigation.Timeline.Total.Duration, HistogramTester sees 2
samples instead of the expected 1.

Disable features::kInitialWebUI and features::kWebUIReloadButton by
default in PageLoadMetricsBrowserTest (tests in
PageLoadMetricsBrowserTestWithInitialWebUIParam still explicitly
override them via sub_feature_list_).

Test history:
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/test/chromium/%3A%2F%2Fchrome%2Ftest%5C%3Abrowser_tests%21gtest%3A%3APageLoadMetricsBrowserTest%23InputEventsForFormSubmission

Prevent premature seed data purge and ClearPrefs store race

In SeedReaderWriter, DoScheduledWrite() (called during initial
migration from Local State and CommitPendingWrite()) stops the
timer immediately while posting serialization and file I/O to the
background task runner. Because HasPendingWrite() only checks
whether the timer is running, AllowToPurgeSeedDataFromMemory() at
the end of SetUpFieldTrials() could purge the seed bytes from
memory before the background write to the seed file finished on
disk. Track in-flight background writes so seed data remains in
memory until the background file write completes.

Also, in VariationsSeedStore::StoreValidatedSeed() on Android,
check whether a seed is currently empty via
SeedReaderWriter::IsEmpty() rather than calling
VariationsSeedStore::ReadSeedData() so that an empty or missing
previous seed does not trigger ClearPrefs(SeedType::LATEST) and
race with or clobber the newly stored seed, and return kEmpty
when GetSeedDataFromSeedFile() reads an empty seed from disk.

3pp: Fix jrt:/ filesystem in Oracle GraalVM native-images

With Oracle GraalVM, jdk.internal.jrtfs.SystemImage's static
initializer runs at image build time, which bakes in the path to the
build machine's GraalVM lib/modules. This caused custom_d8 (and
kotlinc-graalvm) to fail on bots with:
  NoSuchFileException: .../3pp/wd/.../.graalvm/.../lib/modules

Move the SystemImage patch from //third_party/jdk/3pp into graalvm.py,
and apply it to all images that set -H:+AllowJRTFileSystem: patch
findHome() to return java.home, and initialize the class at run time.
Also fail the build if the GraalVM's lib/modules path ends up in the
binary.

[WebUI Toolbar] Paint the pressed tint in the IPH pulse

In native views, the help bubble anchor-highlights its anchor button, so
during an IPH the ink drop shows the pressed ripple on top of the
attention highlight, and both pulse together under one mask. The WebUI
pulse only painted the attention color, so it looked lighter and bluer
than native.

The floating WebUI help bubble does not anchor-highlight WebUI elements,
so instead of wiring that up (which would also trigger each control's
onHighlightChanged side effects, e.g. click suppression and
is-menu-open), paint native's composition directly in the pulsing
::before of help_bubble_anchor.css:
- background-color: the attention color (bottom).
- background-image: the control's pressed color (top), matching
  native, where InkDropImpl::RecreateRippleAndHighlight() stacks the
  ripple above the highlight.

Screenshots: 
https: //issues.chromium.org/issues/572066807#comment3 (and comment 4)

[Omnibox] Update bug triage doc for automated triage

New public Omnibox and Search bugs are now triaged by a public
Buganizer triage playbook that routes them to the Omnibox Core or
Search Inputs & Suggest team inbox. This updates the triage doc to
match:

- Describe what the triage agent does: skips, mobile, out-of-scope
  handling, duplicates, team routing (including the WebUI omnibox
  flag rule), priority and type checks, and the review / Needs Human
  hotlists.
- The agent explains every change in a public comment, and adds
  Needs Human only to bugs it couldn't route. Triagers remove Needs
  Human once they've acted on a bug.
- Replace the M/W/F manual scan and Tuesday keyword search with a
  daily on-call digest. List its sections (Needs Human, restricted,
  could not finish, not picked up, keyword sweep, routed) and what
  the on-call does with each; setup details live in internal docs.
- Add the team inbox and agent hotlists to the quick reference, as
  named links.
- Note that Restrict-View-Google hides a bug from the agent, and how
  to triage such bugs by hand.
- Move the Available / Needs-* hotlists into a Legacy process
  section, since those hotlists are being retired, and drop the
  Tuesday Needs-Feedback review. The hotlists are shared across
  Chromium, so link to searches filtered to the Omnibox and Search
  components. Triage guidance now says to ask for
  missing info in a comment instead of adding Needs-Feedback /
  Needs-TestConfirmation.
- Collapse the manual triage guidance into a short routing section:
  the triage engineer oversees routing, routes each bug as best they
  can, and may fix anything obviously off (e.g. priority). Keep the
  priority guidance and subcomponent table; drop purpose, status,
  owners, labels and the NextAction note. Duplicates of commonly
  reported bugs are now caught by the agent.
- Drop the expired Monorail migration notes and the Search backlog
  catch-up TODO.

[views] Skip SetWindowDisplayAffinity for unchanged or hidden windows

Since crrev.com/c/7982006, showing a widget applies its display affinity
to all windows it owns and to native menus on the UI thread, even when
the affinity is WDA_NONE.

Calling SetWindowDisplayAffinity() causes DWM to render certain hidden
windows as blank rectangles. This notably manifests as a persistent
white box in the top-left corner on systems running third-party
overlays/hooks such as ASUS Smart Input.

To fix this:
- Only call SetWindowDisplayAffinity() when the target affinity differs from
  the current affinity, making this a no-op in the common WDA_NONE case.
- Skip hidden owned windows, as hidden Chromium widgets will apply the
  affinity upon being shown.

[PM] Make BG loads yield to active tab loads in LoadingPageVoter V2

Background loads boosted to kUserVisible still slow down kUserBlocking
loads in the active tab.

With kPMLoadingPageVoterV2:
- Background loads aren't boosted while a load is in progress in an
  active tab. In case that load never finishes, they stop yielding to it
  after 30 seconds.
- kLoadedBusy is no longer considered loading, since it can last up to a
  minute and isn't necessarily related to the load.

kPMLoadingPageVoter is unchanged.

parent
dcf9cd29389b8b9058f414f8d685563fac234283 [ diff ] 
Override InsecureDnsMode via NetworkServiceParams

Overriding via ConfigureStubHostResolver can only be done after the
NetworkService has been created. This can end up causing churn. For
example: invalidating caches, aborting hostname resolution jobs, etc.
Moreover, it seems that WebView ends up creating the NetworkService on
the UI thread, so all of this churn will contend with WebView's startup,
potentially regressing it.

To circumvent this entirely, override InsecureDnsMode via
NetworkServiceParams instead. This makes it so the stub host resolver is
directly created with the right configuration.

Note: this change stops setting happy_eyeballs_v3_enabled=false. This is
intended. The underlying value of happy_eyeballs_v3_enabled is not
changing since it's default disabled. The previous code simply had to set
a value due to ConfigureStubHostResolver requiring it.

c452492b3c98a91fddaf6685c5a99688c6e70223 [ diff ] 
[iOS] Remove currentUIBlocker check in TaskUpdaterSceneAgent

sceneState.profileState.currentUIBlocker indicates whether a scene is
blocking other scenes, not whether the current scene itself is blocked.
Checking currentUIBlocker in -[TaskUpdaterSceneAgent canUpdateToUIReady]
risks blocking the scene that is not actually blocked (i.e. the scene
owning the UI blocker).

Whether the current scene is blocked by another scene's modal overlay is
already checked via sceneState.uiBlockerState.presentingModalOverlay,
matching the legacy -[SceneController canHandleIntents] flow.

[iOS] Guard Duo simulator orientation reset for startup tests

Startup tests launch the app with kPrepareUI, meaning the UI is halted
and no key window exists during setUp. Attempting to rotate or reset
the Duo simulator orientation via HID events in setUp fails because
EarlGrey cannot wait for the key window to settle.

TearDown already guards this with ![ChromeTestCase isStartupTest].
This CL adds the same guard to setUp.

Reland "[a11y] Remove spurious a11y triggers on Android"

This reverts commit c1a570479cdedd2027fc0908de10a3445b65c66f.

Reason for reland: Scope the no-service guard to auto-disable candidate
instances (Chrome browser tabs) so non-candidate embedders such as
WebView continue initializing ui::kAXModeBasic for UiAutomator CTS
tests (CtsInputMethodTestCases).

Original change's description:
> [a11y] Remove spurious a11y triggers on Android
>
> When Android's UiAutomation is connected (e.g. via UIAutomator),
> AccessibilityManager.isEnabled() returns true even though no
> accessibility services are enabled in getEnabledAccessibilityServiceList().
> Previously, a view-hierarchy query on ContentView caused
> WebContentsAccessibilityImpl.getAccessibilityNodeProviderCompat() to
> lazily initialize WebContentsAccessibilityAndroid, which unconditionally
> enabled ui::kAXModeBasic in SetBrowserAXMode() and skipped starting the
> 5s AutoDisableAccessibilityHandler timer because isRootManagerConnected()
> was initially false.
>
> These issues are not theoretical, they happened in testing see internal
> b/565076216 for details.
>
> This change:
> 1. Guards getAccessibilityNodeProviderCompat() so it does not initialize
>    or re-enable renderer accessibility when neither an accessibility
>    service nor a password manager (Autofill) is enabled. This alone
>    avoids the UiAutomation case above, so the timer logic is unchanged.
> 2. Passes AccessibilityState.isAnyAccessibilityServiceEnabled() to
>    WebContentsAccessibilityAndroid::SetBrowserAXMode() and does not
>    enable an AXMode when no accessibility services or password managers
>    are running, even when performance filtering is disallowed by policy
>    (addressing TODO(crbug.com/413016129)).
> 3. Restores the AXMode when renderer accessibility is re-enabled after
>    an auto-disable. DisableRendererAccessibility() clears it and nothing
>    restored it, so the root manager could fail to reconnect.
>
> Tests check the AXMode directly via a new HasScopedAXModeForTesting()
> hook rather than inferring it from the root manager after a DOM change.
>
> AX-Relnotes: no user-visible change.
> Bug: 413016129, 565076216

Adds metrics to track impressions, user interactions, and promo outcomes
for the new Magic Stack Tips V2 cards (NTP Theme, Tips Notifications,

  promo.

  tip.

Don't hold references to name or id across UpdateName()/UpdateId()

Element::InsertedInto() took a const AtomicString& reference into the
element's attribute storage via GetNameAttribute() and passed it to
UpdateName(). UpdateName() calls HTMLDocument::AddNamedItem(), which
initializes the frame's WindowProxy before calling NamedItemAdded().
Initializing a sandboxed frame's script context installs
chrome.loadTimes, which can invoke a page-defined setter on a child
frame named 'chrome'. If that setter mutates the element's attributes
and reallocates the attribute vector, the name_value reference dangles
when NamedItemAdded() reads it.

This CL copies the name and id attributes into local AtomicStrings by
value before calling UpdateName() and UpdateId() in InsertedInto(),
RemovedFrom(), and CloneAttributesFrom().

[wdspec] Fix preload script execution order test for inline script

- Fix the preload script execution order test when a new popup runs an
  inline script, and mark multi-case wdspec tests that exceed the
  default timeout under CI load as slow.
- Previously, the popup subtest opened a top-level `data:` URL from
  script. Chrome blocks script-initiated top-level `data:` navigations,
  which the Fetch specification allows, so the popup never emitted
  `browsingContext.load` and timed out.
- Serve the popup document over HTTP(S) with `inline()` while keeping
  the `data:` URL for the iframe variant.

PrivateAI: Avoid string and protobuf copies

`ReceiveTextRequest` previously copied the `text.value()` string when
passing it to the callback, despite `text` being an optional going out
of scope. Additionally, `ReceiveGenerateContentResponse` and
`ReceivePaicMessage` implicitly copied large nested protobuf messages by
passing const references to the callback.

This CL updates the callbacks to use `std::move` to transfer ownership
of the string and mutable nested protobuf fields. This eliminates deep
copies of strings and potentially large payload protobufs (such as
`GenerateContentResponse`) upon receiving Private AI responses.

This CL was prepared with the help of an AI agent (Kaizen Chrome); the
author reviewed and verified it.
